newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on lower oil demand.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on lower oil demand.

text.p: The Philippine peso firmed up at the close on Monday after local oil companies bought lesser dollars than expected, traders said.
The peso ended at 26.327 from Friday's 26.337. "The market earlier expected oil firms to buy $42 million so the dollar opened higher," said one trader in a foreign bank.
The peso opened at 26.34 on rumour oil firms were planning to buy $42 million.
However, oil firms bought only $26 million at 26.25 to 26.329 at midsession, the traders said.
The Central Bank kept its hands off the market, although it quoted a bid of 26.29 pesos to a dollar and offered to sell at 26.345 to the dollar.
Volume rose to $212.5 million from the previous $183.30 while the average reached 26.328 pesos to a dollar from 26.34.

Traders said the market will take its cue from the Central Bank's action on Tuesday following the drop in the benchmark 91-day treasury bill rate to 10.746 percent in this afternoon's auction from the previous 11.172. --DOLLY AGLAY 841-89-36
